_meta.purpose: Structured resume data for davepack.dev. Skills are normalized in `skills` and referenced by id from `experience`, `projects`, and `stories`, so the site can render by job, by skill, or by timeline without duplicating copy.

conventions.dates: YYYY-MM, or null when current/unknown. `end: null` with `current: true` means ongoing.
conventions.voice: `highlights` and per-job `usage` blurbs are in neutral resume voice (no pronouns). `profile.summary`, `stories`, and `principles` are first person, written for the site.
conventions.proficiency: 1 = familiar, 2 = productive, 3 = strong, 4 = expert / could teach it, 5 = deep specialty.
conventions.featured: Skills and entries with `featured: false` are historical or minor; include for completeness (search, timeline) but keep out of the headline views.
conventions.verify: Fields marked `"verify": true` or values of null are inferred or unknown and should be confirmed by Dave before publishing.

profile.name: Dave Pack
profile.headline: Full-Stack Software Engineer · Web Platform Lead
profile.summaryShort: Full-stack engineer: 15 years building for the web, 11 shipping products in JavaScript, React, and Node. Web Platform Lead for Kroger's e-commerce site. Daily practitioner of AI-native development.
profile.summary: I'm a full-stack engineer with 15 years building for the web and 11 shipping production software in JavaScript, React, and Node. For the last eight years I've been Web Platform Lead for Kroger's e-commerce site, where I lead a four-developer platform team that owns architecture, performance, and code quality for a codebase shared by more than twenty teams and serving over eleven million weekly visitors. I influence through collaboration rather than authority: architecture and standards boards, ADRs, and a lot of pairing. I like modernizing legacy systems while keeping them stable, and I practice AI-native development every day with Claude Code.

stories.title: Skipping two major versions: the React Router migration
stories.context: Kroger's e-commerce app was on React Router v5 with a home-grown, partially config-based routing system and a home-built SSR server. I'm leading the migration to React Router 7 framework mode.
stories.problem: The conventional path is v5, then the v5-to-v6 compat package, then v6, then v7. Working through that path with Claude, I found it was full of blockers and throwaway migration code because of how unusual our legacy routing system was.
stories.action: I paused to explore the codebase more deeply, and with Claude's help discovered that because our routing was already partially config-based, we could rework it to be fully config-based and match the React Router 7 API while still on v5.
stories.result: That lets us skip the compat package and v6 entirely, unblocking the migration and saving a significant amount of throwaway code. I've since used AI daily to implement the migration, and my workflow evolves every time I enter a prompt.
stories.takeaway: This is what I think AI-native engineering is for: not only generating code faster, but exploring and validating a better path than the one you walked in with.

stories.title: Leaving behind a tech lead
stories.context: I joined Kroger as a team contributor and became tech lead in my first year.
stories.problem: A tech lead who is the only person who can lead is a bottleneck, and a team that can't survive its lead leaving isn't healthy.
stories.action: As tech lead I spent a lot of time pairing with teammates and preparing them to lead: sharing context, handing over responsibility a little before they felt ready, and trusting them with it.
stories.result: I moved to lead other teams twice, and both times left behind an engineer who was prepared to step into the tech lead role of the team I was leaving.
stories.takeaway: I love pairing and learning in both directions. Trusting people with responsibility before they think they're ready is how they become ready.

principles.title: Influence through collaboration
principles.blurb: Architecture boards, standards boards, ADRs, and pairing beat mandates. Standards that people helped write are standards people follow.

principles.title: Modernize without breaking production
principles.blurb: Large legacy systems exist because they worked. Improve them incrementally, keep them stable, and respect the teams that maintain them.

principles.title: Leave teams better than you found them
principles.blurb: The measure of leading a team is what happens after you step back. Prepare the next lead while you're still there.

principles.title: AI as a thinking partner, not just a typist
principles.blurb: The biggest wins from AI-native development have come from exploring and validating better paths, not from typing faster.

principles.title: Empathy for the user
principles.blurb: Talk to users, prototype, test, and sweat the details that make an interface feel right.
